title: The Real Effects of Fair Workweek Laws on Work Schedules: Evidence from Los Angeles
eligible_reason: Single policy date: Los Angeles' Fair Workweek Law effective 1 April 2023; treated workers/stores in LA city vs non-LA stores of the same seven retail chains. month_to_la is event time relative to that common date (calendar weeks containing 2023-04-01), post = month_to_la >= 1. Main Table 3: feols(log(advance_notice_mean) ~ la_city*post | company^unit_skey + company^assigned_to_7 + company^month_to_la); col 1 has no controls, cols 2-5 add log hours/shift/demand/supply/operating/edit-count controls. Event study (Figure 2a) i(month_to_la, la_city, 0) with controls. No staggered adoption, and the restricted data are not shipped.
design_notes: R/fixest sanitized script main_workers_VERIFICATION_sanitized.R: Table 3 lines 368-372, Figure 2a line 354, Table 4 heterogeneity (triple interactions with wage, part_time, male), Table 5 stability, Table 6 worker outcomes, Table 7 store-level outcomes (feols and fepois). Clustering company^unit_skey and month_to_la^company.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: LA FWL effective 2023-04-01 for all treated units.

specs.exclusion_reason: single common treatment date (not staggered); data not shipped
